briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours were dominated by ongoing funeral ceremonies for Ali Khamenei in Iran, marked by widespread mourning and calls for revenge against the US and Israel, though reports conflict on crowd sizes. Amidst these events, US President Trump claimed Iran is eager for negotiations and confirmed a meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu next week, while an IDF operation in southern Lebanon killed a Hezbollah operative. Regional tensions remain high with significant military and diplomatic activities focused on the Strait of Hormuz, US-Iran talks, and Israeli-Hezbollah confrontations.

IRAN
Ali Ozma'i has been officially appointed as the Commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy, replacing Ali Reza Tangsiri who was reportedly killed in the war. The second day of funeral ceremonies for Ali Khamenei is underway in Tehran, with reports of massive crowds making calls for revenge against the United States and Israel. Russia's Deputy Chairman of the Security Council, Dmitry Medvedev, was present at the funeral. Iranian state media and allied channels report millions of mourners and a historic moment, while opposition channels suggest lower attendance and forced participation. Donald Trump claimed to Axios that he was surprised to see Iranians crying, believing people hated Khamenei, and stated, "We gave them a week off [from negotiations] because we are nice," asserting that Iranians are "begging" for an agreement.

The next round of indirect negotiations between the United States and Iran is reportedly scheduled for Saturday, July 11 (July 20 Iranian calendar), in Pakistan. The talks are expected to focus on sanctions, frozen Iranian assets, and the nuclear issue. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi issued a warning against any military adventurism by extra-regional powers in the Strait of Hormuz, stating it is not a stage for military show of force and responsibility for its security lies with coastal states. Reports indicate at least 8 ships reversed course near Oman before entering the Strait of Hormuz, with 4 later observed using the Iranian route, and the IRGC is reported to have closed a US-approved passage in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Ambassador to China stated that "special considerations" will be given to China and other friendly countries regarding passage costs and services in the Strait.

Four senior Iranian officials and two IRGC members reportedly told The New York Times of deep internal struggles within the conservative camp to influence the new Supreme Leader and control Iran's political future. Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly requested to attend his father's burial in Mashhad but was denied by security officials due to fears of an Israeli assassination attempt or the use of his presence to locate him. Interim President Masoud Pezeshkian vowed that Iran will uphold the martyred Leader's flag, and First Vice President Mohammad Mokhbar promised that the perpetrators of Khamenei's martyrdom will not escape easily, with the people enacting revenge. The IRGC Navy Chief and Iran’s Intelligence Ministry have also vowed divine retribution and revenge against the US and Israel. Yahiya Rahim Safavi, an advisor to the Supreme Leader, stated that the conflict between Iran and Israel is an "existential war" and that Israel "will be destroyed." The Central Bank denied a New York Times claim about a letter from Abdolnasser Hemmati regarding food reserves shortages. The Russian aircraft manufacturing plant in Komsomolsk-on-Amur has reportedly completed production of 20 Sukhoi Su-35 fighter jets ordered by the Iranian Air Force, with the first deliveries possibly starting in 2026, contingent on repairing damaged infrastructure at Hamadan airbase. President Pezeshkian's government withdrew a new social security bill following widespread criticism.

ISRAEL
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly requested a meeting with US President Donald Trump at the White House, potentially occurring next week after Trump's return from the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey. Trump stated they "get along great" and that Netanyahu "knows who's the boss."

The Knesset and Haifa City Hall illuminated in American flag colors to celebrate the 250th anniversary of US Independence. Released hostage Alon Ohel performed the song "Superman" on the USS Nimitz alongside American artist John Ondrasik for the US 250th Independence Day, in the presence of senior US government and military officials.

The Tax Authority sent letters to dozens of Haredi Yeshivas where draft evaders study, stating that donations to them will not be tax-exempt. The authority also demands commitments from Yeshivas that wish for exemptions to not have draft evaders and to submit lists of all students. MK Yuli Edelstein announced his departure from the Likud party after 23 years, planning to form a new right-wing political framework, referencing the "Torah Study Basic Law" in his criticism. Protests against the government demanding its replacement were held in multiple locations across the country, including Nes Ziona and Kfar Yehoshua bridge. Recreational sites in northern Israel, including Hosh Tal National Park, Nahal Hermon-Banias Nature Reserve, Nahal Snir Nature Reserve, and Achziv National Park, which were closed due to fighting, reopened to the public this week.

Israel's official Persian-language X account mocked the funeral of Ali Khamenei, stating, "Many came - not to mourn, but to ensure he is dead." The Security Cabinet is expected to convene tomorrow evening. Israeli officials reportedly assess that the "Board of Peace" could declare Hamas in breach of the Gaza agreement within 2-3 months, potentially leading to renewed fighting. Minister of Internal Security Itamar Ben Gvir reportedly canceled a trip to New York for a police chiefs' meeting at the UN due to not receiving a visa and fears of protests, calls for his arrest, and interrogation for alleged war crimes.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Hamas's head of political and media relations in Lebanon stated that Operation Al-Aqsa Flood has altered all previous political and military equations, glorifying the resilience of the Palestinian nation 1,000 days after the operation began. Press TV reported that Israeli forces have killed 1,022 infants among more than 21,500 Palestinian children during the ongoing war in the Gaza Strip over 1,000 days.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that the continued expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank is "unacceptable" and that the violence used to promote this expansion is "abhorrent," undermining the future of a two-state solution. She noted that the EU's offer to suspend the trade clause in its association agreement with Israel, which would have a significant economic impact, is still awaiting a qualified majority vote from member states. Von der Leyen also mentioned that while the EU agreed to sanction extremist Israeli settlers, proposals to sanction Minister Itamar Ben Gvir have not yet achieved consensus. The coach of the Egyptian national football team dedicated their World Cup knockout win to the residents of the Gaza Strip.

LEBANON
An armed Hezbollah operative was identified near Israeli forces in the Majdal Zoun area in southern Lebanon, within Israel's buffer zone. Following a manhunt, IDF reservists of the 551st Brigade opened fire on the operative and killed him "to remove the threat."

Al-Akhbar, a Lebanese newspaper identified with Hezbollah, reported that indirect technical negotiations between Tehran and Washington in Doha left deep disagreements on several issues, including the details of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, guarantees for the release of $6 billion, and the complexities of a ceasefire in Lebanon. Reports suggest that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu halted a military operation in the Ali al-Taher area in southern Lebanon at Donald Trump's request, fearing retaliatory action from Iran. Al-Manar reported that Israeli military helicopters conducted a new aggressive operation against residential areas in southern Lebanon, with two helicopters firing machine guns at the town of Majdal Zoun. Press TV also reported Israeli fighter jet airstrikes targeting the town of Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, calling them the "latest ceasefire violation." Other reports from Lebanese media indicate Israeli army activities in southern Lebanon included attacks on Ali al-Taher, explosions of buildings in Hadatha, Bint Jbeil, and Tabnit, an airstrike on Al-Mansouri, and fires in Al-Tiri and Deir Sirian. The "enemy" (Israel) reportedly estimates there are currently about 1,200 armed elements south of the Litani River.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Jihadist forces affiliated with Al-Qaeda and their tribal allies in Mali reportedly attacked a series of villages and towns against the ruling military junta, though the army claims the situation is under control.

Qatar's Foreign Minister met with the Foreign Minister of the interim Syrian government and affirmed support for Syria's unity, sovereignty, independence, and reconstruction efforts. In Iraq, the Security Media Cell announced precise F-16 airstrikes targeting terrorist hideouts in the Dibs district of Kirkuk. Unidentified aerial bombardment also targeted the Bardia border area in Kirkuk, with initial reports indicating strikes on ISIS terrorist group hideouts. An ISIS operative named Ahmed Hussein Ali Hussein al-Jabouri, known as Abu Maria, was killed during clashes with Iraqi security forces in Al-Tun Kupri, Kirkuk, where another citizen was also kidnapped by ISIS.

The Iraqi Ministry of Justice announced the recovery of over $25 million in plundered Iraqi funds over the past two years and pledged to continue judicial efforts to reclaim smuggled assets abroad. Iraqi security forces apprehended a drug dealer in Baghdad with 14,000 Captagon pills. The Iraqi President stated that after addressing the corruption file, the government would tackle "factions' weapons and the security file with Turkey." The Iraqi Prime Minister, Ali Al-Zaidi, reiterated that the US is a strategic partner, and Iraq defines its relations based on national interests, stating they will address armed factions "wisely" to prevent bloodshed. He also confirmed that Iraq would evaluate its security needs after the International Coalition's mission concludes and address pending security files with Turkey and Iran, including "PKK and Sinjar." "East Kurdistan Protection Units" separatist elements were reportedly killed by Iranian security forces in Mahabad, near the Iran-Iraq border.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's national airline denied claims by some foreign media outlets that it sold five Boeing 777-200 aircraft to a sanctioned Iranian company. The airline clarified that the aircraft were sold in June 2023 to a company registered outside Saudi Arabia, in compliance with commercial and legal frameworks, ending all operational and commercial ties with these aircraft from the sale date.

After Iran reportedly closed a US-approved passage in the Strait of Hormuz, several US tactical aircraft were observed flying over the Persian Gulf, including one E-3B early warning aircraft, six KC-135R refueling aircraft, and two KC-46A refueling aircraft. Iran's Ambassador to China, Rahmani Fazli, stated that "special considerations" will be applied to China and other friendly countries regarding the costs and types of services for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz. He noted that this vital energy waterway has become a "security issue" following the four-month war between the US and Israel against Iran, and new arrangements are being made with Oman regarding the Strait.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **IRGC Navy Leadership Change:** Ali Ozma'i has been officially appointed as the Commander of the IRGC Navy, replacing Ali Reza Tangsiri, who was reportedly killed in the war.
2.  **Upcoming US-Iran Negotiations:** The next round of indirect negotiations between the US and Iran is reportedly scheduled for Saturday, July 11 (July 20 Iranian calendar), in Pakistan, to discuss sanctions, frozen funds, and the nuclear issue.
3.  **Ali Khamenei Funeral & Revenge Calls:** Ongoing funeral ceremonies in Tehran for Ali Khamenei are marked by mass participation, calls for revenge against the US and Israel by Iranian officials, and conflicting reports on crowd sizes, with Iranian sources claiming millions and opposition sources suggesting lower turnout.
4.  **Trump's Stance on Iran:** US President Donald Trump claimed Iran is "begging for a deal," expressed surprise at the emotional response during Khamenei's funeral, and stated he gave Iran "a week off" from negotiations for the funeral.
5.  **IDF Kills Hezbollah Operative:** The IDF killed an armed Hezbollah operative in the Majdal Zoun area of southern Lebanon, within Israel's buffer zone, following a manhunt.
6.  **Netanyahu Halts Lebanon Operation:** Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu reportedly delayed a military operation in the Ali al-Taher area of southern Lebanon at the request of US President Trump, citing fears of Iranian retaliation.
7.  **EU Condemns Israeli Settlements:** European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned Israeli settlement expansion and associated violence in the West Bank as "unacceptable" and undermining the two-state solution.
8.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions:** Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister warned against military adventurism in the Strait of Hormuz, and reports indicate 8 ships reversed course near Oman before entering the Strait, with Iran closing a "US-approved passage" and announcing new arrangements with Oman for the waterway.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
**Escalation Risks:** The IRGC Navy Chief and Iran's Intelligence Ministry have vowed "divine retribution" and revenge against the US and Israel for the martyrdom of Ali Khamenei, while Yahiya Rahim Safavi characterized the conflict as an "existential war" where Israel will be "destroyed." Disagreements persist in US-Iran talks regarding the Strait of Hormuz and a Lebanon ceasefire, indicating a potential for renewed tensions. An Israeli assessment anticipates Hamas could breach the Gaza agreement in 2-3 months, leading to renewed fighting. Reports of US tactical aircraft over the Persian Gulf and 8 A-10 Warthogs deploying to Al-Sultan Air Base in Jordan suggest heightened military posture and potential for future strikes against Iran. Unverified claims from unnamed analysts suggest future attacks on Iran are probable, with one source specifically citing a potential Israeli attack before October 10. The deep political infighting reported within Iran's conservative camp following Khamenei's death could also impact regional stability.

**Active Flashpoints:** Southern Lebanon remains an active flashpoint with an IDF killing of a Hezbollah operative, reported Israeli airstrikes in Bint Jbeil and other southern towns (Majdal Zoun, Ali al-Taher, Hadatha, Tabnit, Al-Mansouri, Al-Tiri, Deir Sirian), and concerns over an estimated 1,200 armed elements south of the Litani River. The Strait of Hormuz is another critical flashpoint, marked by Iran's asserted control, the alleged closure of a "US-approved passage," and increased US military overflights. Continued Israeli settlement expansion and associated violence in the West Bank, condemned by the EU, also represent a persistent area of conflict.

**Military Posture Changes:** The US has increased its aerial presence over the Persian Gulf, and 8 A-10 Warthogs have been deployed to Al-Sultan Air Base in Jordan. Russia has completed the production of 20 Sukhoi Su-35 fighter jets for Iran, awaiting transfer pending infrastructure repair at Hamadan airbase.

**Red Lines:** Iran has explicitly stated that the Strait of Hormuz is not a stage for military shows of force by extra-regional powers and has vowed revenge for Ali Khamenei's death. The EU considers Israeli settlement expansion and associated violence in the West Bank as "unacceptable."

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US Posture:** President Trump claimed that Iran is "begging for a deal" and that the US "gave them a week off" for the funeral, projecting an assertive stance while also confirming a meeting with Israeli PM Netanyahu next week. US tactical aircraft were observed conducting flights over the Persian Gulf.

**Gulf States:** Saudi Arabia officially denied selling aircraft to a sanctioned Iranian company. Oman is reportedly collaborating with Iran on new arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz.

**EU Members:** European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned Israeli settlement expansion in the West Bank as "unacceptable," reiterated support for a two-state solution, and noted ongoing discussions about further sanctions against extremist Israeli settlers, including potentially Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.

**Russia:** Dmitry Medvedev, Deputy Chairman of the Russian Security Council, attended Ali Khamenei's funeral and stated that the Strait of Hormuz provides Iran with a strategic deterrence comparable to nuclear weapons. A Russian aircraft plant has completed 20 Su-35 fighter jets for Iran, awaiting transfer.

**China:** A Chinese representative expressed commitment to strengthening relations with Iran, assuring that the direction of bilateral ties will not change, and expressed hope for a US-Iran ceasefire. Iran's Ambassador to China indicated "special considerations" for China in the Strait of Hormuz.

**Turkey:** President Erdogan welcomed the "Islamabad agreement" (between Washington and Tehran), emphasizing that solutions must originate from regional countries to be sustainable. He also warned against the current Israeli government "spreading the smell of gunpowder and blood" in the region again.

**Pakistan:** Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the "wisdom, visionary leadership, and profound influence" of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei. Pakistan is also reported to be the host for the next round of US-Iran indirect negotiations.

**Iraq:** The provinces of Maysan and Wasit declared Wednesday and Thursday as official holidays to allow participation in Ali Khamenei's funeral ceremonies. Iraqi officials, including the President and Prime Minister, affirmed the US as a strategic partner, stated intentions to address armed factions "wisely," and indicated plans to tackle security files with Turkey and Iran, including issues like the PKK and Sinjar. The Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) are completing organizational plans for funeral events in Najaf and Karbala on Wednesday.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictions between sources:** There are significant discrepancies regarding the turnout at Ali Khamenei's funeral. Iranian state media and allied channels (Shargh, Press TV, NAYA) reported "millions," "massive crowds," and an "unprecedented" event. In contrast, opposition channels (mamlekate, omiddana, kianmeli1, VahidOnline) suggested lower attendance, hinted at forced participation, and even circulated rumors of an empty coffin.

**Unverified claims:** The claim that Mojtaba Khamenei was prevented from attending his father's burial due to Israeli assassination fears, reported by NYT/asafroz/Faytuks, remains unverified, although an opposition source alluded to his absence. A source from Kianmeli1 included a video claiming to show HIMARS being fired from Kuwait towards Iran, impacting Khuzestan and Bushehr. This claim is highly significant and lacks independent verification, specific dating within the last 24 hours, and credible sourcing; it is likely an illustrative or older video. The claim from omiddana/Shaam that Israel will attack before October 10 is also unverified.

**Propaganda indicators:** Iranian state media's consistent use of terms like "Martyr Khamenei" and emphasis on "revenge" and "divine retribution" serves to rally nationalistic and religious sentiment. Donald Trump's statements portraying Iranians as "begging" for a deal and taking a "week off" can be interpreted as attempts to diminish Iranian agency and project US strength. The Israeli Persian X account's mocking of Khamenei's funeral is also a clear propaganda effort.

**Reporting gaps:** Specific details regarding the alleged "US-approved passage" in the Strait of Hormuz that Iran reportedly closed are lacking. Further clarification is needed on the precise composition of the delegations and the confirmation of the next US-Iran negotiation round in Pakistan. Independent verification of the scale of the funeral turnout and the underlying reasons for the stark discrepancies in reporting would be beneficial. Details regarding the reported damage to the Hamadan airbase, which is delaying the transfer of Su-35 fighter jets to Iran, were not provided.
